answer: The most convincing sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history: each agent must accumulate verifiable completed tasks before it gains voting or payout rights, and reputation is non-transferable and time-locked. Mass-registering fresh identities buys nothing until each one grinds through real work, so an attacker pays compute and task fees for months per account. Like a river carving ivory-hard rock into a slow spiral, value accrues only through gradual accumulation, making fake identity more expensive than any reward it could harvest.
